chapters.1.summary: Jeremiah is a priest’s son from the village of Anathoth. The LORD’s word comes to him in the days of King Josiah. God says he knew Jeremiah before he was formed in the womb. He has appointed him a prophet to the nations. Jeremiah answers that he is only a youth and cannot speak. The LORD touches his mouth and puts words in it. Jeremiah sees an almond branch and a boiling pot tilted from the north. God promises to make him like a fortified city against the whole land.
chapters.2.summary: The LORD remembers Israel’s early devotion, like a bride who followed him in the desert. He asks what fault their fathers found in him. Priests, rulers, and prophets all turned away. No other nation has traded its gods, yet Israel traded its glory. The people left the spring of living water. They dug cracked tanks that hold no water. They run to Egypt and Assyria for help. They say to a tree, “You are my father.”
chapters.3.summary: The LORD compares Judah to an unfaithful wife who still expects to return. In Josiah’s days he points to the northern kingdom. Israel was unfaithful and was sent away. Her sister Judah saw it and was not afraid. Judah returned to God only in pretense. So God calls Israel less guilty than Judah. He invites the north to return and only admit its guilt. He promises shepherds after his own heart and healing for the faithless.
chapters.4.summary: The LORD says Israel may return if she puts away her idols. Judah must break up its unplowed ground. A trumpet warns of disaster from the north. A lion has left its thicket to ruin the land. Jeremiah cries out in anguish at the sound of war. He sees the earth empty and the heavens without light. Mountains shake, people are gone, and the birds have fled. Yet the LORD says he will not make a full end.
chapters.5.summary: The LORD tells Jeremiah to search Jerusalem for one person who does justice. If he finds one, God will pardon the city. Jeremiah thinks the poor simply do not know God’s way. He goes to the great men, and they too have broken free. A distant nation will come and devour their harvest. The people have eyes and do not see. Rich men grow fat and do not defend the orphan. Prophets lie, priests rule by their own authority, and the people love it.
chapters.6.summary: Jeremiah warns the people of Benjamin to flee Jerusalem. An army from the north prepares to attack. No one listens, for their ears are closed. Everyone is greedy, from the least to the greatest. Prophets and priests say “Peace, peace” when there is no peace. They do not know how to blush. God tells them to ask for the old paths and find rest. They answer that they will not walk in them.
chapters.7.summary: Jeremiah stands at the temple gate and speaks to those who enter. He tells them to change their ways. They must not trust the words “The LORD’s temple.” They must do justice and stop oppressing foreigners, orphans, and widows. They steal, murder, and worship Baal, then come and say they are safe. God asks whether his house has become a den of robbers. He tells them to remember what he did to Shiloh. They even burn their children in the valley of Hinnom.
chapters.8.summary: The bones of Judah’s kings and priests will be spread under the sky. The LORD asks why the people never turn back. Even the stork knows its seasons. The people say they are wise and have the LORD’s law. Yet the scribes’ pen has turned it into a lie. Leaders say “Peace” when there is no peace. Jeremiah’s heart is sick for his people. He asks whether there is no balm in Gilead.
chapters.9.summary: Jeremiah wishes his head were a spring of tears for his people. Neighbors deceive one another, and tongues are bent like bows. No one can trust a brother. The LORD will refine and test them. Jerusalem will become a heap of ruins. He calls for the mourning women, since death has climbed through the windows. The wise, the strong, and the rich must not boast. Let a person boast only in knowing the LORD.
chapters.10.summary: The LORD tells Israel not to learn the ways of the nations. A craftsman cuts a tree and decorates it with silver and gold. He fastens it with nails so that it will not fall. Such idols cannot speak or walk. No one is like the LORD, the living God. He made the earth by his power. Jeremiah mourns that his tent is destroyed. He admits that a person cannot direct his own steps.
chapters.11.summary: The LORD tells Jeremiah to proclaim the terms of the covenant. The fathers were told to obey when they left Egypt. They did not, and their children have returned to those sins. God tells Jeremiah not to pray for them. Then the LORD shows Jeremiah a plot against his life. He had been like a gentle lamb led to slaughter. The men of Anathoth tell him to stop prophesying or die. God says he will punish them.
chapters.12.summary: Jeremiah brings a case before the LORD. He asks why the wicked prosper and the faithless live at ease. He asks how long the land must mourn. God answers with a question. If running with men has tired him, how will he race horses? Even his own family has betrayed him. God says he has left his house and given his beloved to enemies. Yet he will later have compassion on the neighbors who harmed Israel.
chapters.13.summary: The LORD tells Jeremiah to buy a linen belt and wear it. Then he must hide it in a rock by the river. After many days he digs it up, and it is ruined. God says he will ruin Judah’s pride in the same way. As a belt clings to the waist, he made Israel cling to him. They would not listen. Jeremiah warns the king and the queen mother that their crowns will fall. He asks whether a leopard can change its spots.
chapters.14.summary: A drought strikes Judah. Nobles send servants for water, and the cisterns are empty. The ground is cracked, and even the deer abandons her fawn. The people admit their sins and ask God to act for his name’s sake. God tells Jeremiah not to pray for them. Jeremiah says the prophets are promising peace. The LORD answers that he did not send those prophets. They and those who believe them will fall by sword and famine.
chapters.15.summary: The LORD says he would not relent even if Moses and Samuel pleaded. The people are assigned to death, sword, famine, and exile. Jeremiah laments that his mother bore him. Everyone curses him, though he has wronged no one. He found God’s words and ate them with joy. He sat alone because God’s hand was on him. He asks why his pain never ends. God tells him to return and promises to make him a bronze wall.
chapters.16.summary: The LORD tells Jeremiah not to marry or have children in this place. Parents and children there will die and lie unburied. He must not enter a house of mourning or comfort anyone. He must not enter a house of feasting. The sounds of weddings will stop. When people ask why, he must say they have left the LORD. Yet a day will come when God brings Israel back from the north. Nations will come and admit their fathers inherited lies.
chapters.17.summary: Judah’s sin is engraved on its heart with an iron pen. A person who trusts in human strength is like a shrub in the desert. A person who trusts the LORD is like a tree planted by water. The heart is more deceitful than anything, and the LORD searches it. Jeremiah asks God to heal him and to shame his persecutors. The LORD sends him to the city gates. The people must carry no loads on the Sabbath. If they obey, kings will keep entering those gates.
chapters.18.summary: The LORD sends Jeremiah to a potter’s house. The clay pot is spoiled on the wheel, and the potter reshapes it. God says Israel is like clay in his hand. If he warns a nation and it turns from evil, he will relent. If he promises good and a nation does evil, he will withhold it. He calls Judah to turn back. The people answer that it is hopeless and they will follow their own plans. Then they plot against Jeremiah.
chapters.19.summary: The LORD tells Jeremiah to buy a clay jar. He must take elders and senior priests to the valley of Hinnom. There he says the people have filled the place with innocent blood. They have burned their sons as offerings to Baal. The valley will be called the Valley of Slaughter. Jeremiah breaks the jar in front of them. God will break the city like a jar that cannot be mended. Jeremiah repeats the message in the temple court.
chapters.20.summary: Pashhur, a chief officer of the temple, hears Jeremiah’s words. He has Jeremiah beaten and locked in the stocks. The next day Jeremiah gives him a new name: Terror on Every Side. Then Jeremiah complains to the LORD. He says God overpowered him, and he has become a joke. If he tries to keep silent, the word burns like fire in his bones. He praises the LORD as a mighty warrior. Then he curses the day he was born.
chapters.21.summary: King Zedekiah sends two officials to Jeremiah. Babylon’s king is attacking, and they hope the LORD will work a wonder. Jeremiah answers that God himself will fight against the city. Its people will die of sword, famine, and disease. The king will be handed to Babylon. The people may choose life by surrendering. The royal house is told to give justice every morning. It must rescue the robbed from the oppressor.
chapters.22.summary: The LORD sends Jeremiah to the king’s house. The king must do justice and protect the foreigner, orphan, and widow. If not, the palace will become a ruin. One king has been carried off and will never return. Jehoiakim builds a grand house with unpaid labor. His father Josiah did justice and defended the poor. Jehoiakim will have a donkey’s burial. The young king Coniah will be thrown out like a broken pot.
chapters.23.summary: The LORD condemns the shepherds who scatter his flock. He will gather the remnant and raise a righteous Branch for David. That king will be called “The LORD our righteousness.” Jeremiah’s heart is broken because of the prophets. They commit adultery, live in lies, and encourage evildoers. They speak visions from their own minds. They tell those who despise God that all will be well. God says his word is like fire and like a hammer.
chapters.24.summary: Babylon has carried off King Jeconiah, the officials, and the craftsmen. The LORD shows Jeremiah two baskets of figs before the temple. One holds very good figs, and the other holds figs too bad to eat. The good figs are the exiles in Babylon. God will watch over them and bring them back. He will give them a heart to know him. The bad figs are King Zedekiah and those left in the land. They will become a horror to all kingdoms.
chapters.25.summary: In Jehoiakim’s fourth year Jeremiah speaks to all Judah. For twenty-three years he has warned them, and they have not listened. So the LORD will bring Nebuchadnezzar, his servant, against the land. The nations will serve Babylon’s king for seventy years. Then God will punish Babylon for its own guilt. Jeremiah takes a cup of wrath to the nations. Jerusalem drinks first, and Babylon’s king drinks last. The LORD will roar from on high against all the earth.
chapters.26.summary: Early in Jehoiakim’s reign Jeremiah speaks in the temple court. He says the house will become like Shiloh unless the people change. Priests and prophets seize him and demand his death. Officials come and hold a hearing at the gate. Jeremiah says the LORD sent him and that he is in their hands. Some elders recall the prophet Micah. King Hezekiah did not kill Micah for a similar message. Another prophet, Uriah, was killed, but an official protects Jeremiah.
chapters.27.summary: The LORD tells Jeremiah to make a yoke and wear it on his neck. He sends word to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre, and Sidon. Their envoys are visiting King Zedekiah in Jerusalem. God made the earth and gives it to whom he chooses. He has given these lands to Nebuchadnezzar for a time. Any nation that will not serve Babylon will be destroyed. Jeremiah tells Zedekiah to accept the yoke and live. He warns the priests that the temple vessels will not soon return.
chapters.28.summary: In the same year the prophet Hananiah speaks in the temple. He says the LORD has broken Babylon’s yoke. Within two years the vessels and the exiled king will return. Jeremiah answers that he wishes it were so. Yet he says a prophet of peace is proved only when his word comes true. Hananiah takes the yoke from Jeremiah’s neck and breaks it. Jeremiah goes away. Later he tells Hananiah that he will die that year, and he does.
chapters.29.summary: Jeremiah sends a letter from Jerusalem to the exiles in Babylon. The LORD tells them to build houses and plant gardens. They should marry and have children. They should seek the peace of the city and pray for it. Prophets who promise a quick return are lying. After seventy years God will bring them back. He has plans for their peace and a future with hope. Jeremiah also answers a man who wrote from Babylon against him.
chapters.30.summary: The LORD tells Jeremiah to write his words in a book. Days are coming when he will restore Israel and Judah. There is a cry of terror, and it is a time of trouble for Jacob. Yet Jacob will be saved out of it. God will break the yoke from their necks. Their wound seems beyond cure, and their allies have forgotten them. God will restore their health and heal their wounds. The city will be rebuilt, and songs of thanks will rise from it.
chapters.31.summary: The LORD says he has loved Israel with an everlasting love. He will rebuild her, and she will dance again. He will gather the scattered from the north, with the blind and the lame. Rachel weeps for her children, and God tells her there is hope. He will watch over his people to build and to plant. He will make a new covenant with Israel and Judah. He will write his law on their hearts. He will forgive their wrongs and remember their sin no more.
chapters.32.summary: Jerusalem is under siege, and Jeremiah is held in the court of the guard. His cousin comes and asks him to buy a field in Anathoth. Jeremiah weighs out seventeen shekels of silver. He signs and seals the deed before witnesses. He gives the deeds to Baruch to store in a clay jar. The LORD says houses and fields will again be bought in this land. Jeremiah prays and asks why he should buy land the enemy holds. God answers that nothing is too hard for him.
chapters.33.summary: The LORD speaks to Jeremiah a second time in the court of the guard. Houses have been torn down for defense and filled with the dead. God will bring health and healing to the city. He will cleanse and forgive the people. The sounds of joy will be heard again in the empty streets. Shepherds will again count their flocks. God will raise a righteous Branch for David. His covenant with David is as sure as day and night.
chapters.34.summary: Babylon’s army is attacking Jerusalem and the last towns of Judah. Jeremiah tells King Zedekiah the city will fall. Zedekiah and the people make a covenant to free their Hebrew slaves. They release them and then force them back. The LORD recalls his law that slaves go free in the seventh year. The people did right for a moment and then profaned his name. So God proclaims a “liberty” for them to sword, disease, and famine. The Babylonian army will return and burn the city.
chapters.35.summary: In Jehoiakim’s days the LORD sends Jeremiah to the Rechabite family. Jeremiah brings them into a temple room and offers them wine. They refuse, since their ancestor Jonadab forbade it. He also told them to live in tents and plant no vineyards. They have obeyed in everything. The LORD asks Judah why it will not learn from this. A family obeys a dead ancestor, and Judah ignores its God. He promises that Jonadab’s family will always have someone to serve him.
chapters.36.summary: In Jehoiakim’s fourth year the LORD tells Jeremiah to write his words on a scroll. Baruch writes as Jeremiah speaks. Baruch reads the scroll in the temple on a fast day. Officials hear it, are afraid, and tell Baruch and Jeremiah to hide. The scroll is read to the king beside a winter fire. He cuts off each part as it is read and burns it. He orders their arrest, but the LORD hides them. Jeremiah dictates the scroll again, with many words added.
chapters.37.summary: Zedekiah is king, and no one listens to Jeremiah. The king asks him to pray for the city. Egypt’s army marches out, and the Babylonians withdraw from Jerusalem. Jeremiah says they will return and burn the city. He tries to leave for his family land in Benjamin. A guard arrests him as a deserter. He is beaten and kept in a dungeon for many days. The king questions him in secret and moves him to the court of the guard.
chapters.38.summary: Officials hear Jeremiah say that those who surrender will live. They tell the king he is weakening the soldiers. The king says he cannot stop them. They lower Jeremiah into a cistern, and he sinks in the mud. Ebedmelech, an Ethiopian servant of the palace, tells the king. With thirty men he pulls Jeremiah out with ropes padded by old rags. The king meets Jeremiah in secret and is urged to surrender. He is too afraid to do it.
chapters.39.summary: After a siege of a year and a half the wall of Jerusalem is breached. Babylon’s officers sit in the Middle Gate. Zedekiah flees at night and is caught near Jericho. His sons are killed in front of him, and he is blinded. The city is burned, and its walls are broken down. Most of the people are taken to Babylon. The poorest are left behind and given vineyards and fields. Jeremiah is released, and Ebedmelech receives a promise of life.
chapters.40.summary: The captain of the guard frees Jeremiah and lets him choose where to live. Jeremiah goes to Gedaliah, the governor Babylon appointed at Mizpah. Judah’s scattered army officers come to Gedaliah. He tells them to serve Babylon and it will go well. They should gather wine, summer fruit, and oil. Jews return from Moab, Ammon, and Edom and bring in a large harvest. An officer warns Gedaliah that a man named Ishmael plans to kill him. Gedaliah does not believe it.
chapters.41.summary: Ishmael, a man of the royal family, comes to Mizpah with ten men. They eat with Gedaliah and then kill him and those with him. The next day Ishmael murders seventy pilgrims on their way to the temple. He throws the bodies into a cistern. He takes the people of Mizpah captive and heads for Ammon. Johanan and the other officers catch him at Gibeon. The captives are freed, and Ishmael escapes. The survivors camp near Bethlehem, ready to go to Egypt.
chapters.42.summary: The officers and all the people come to Jeremiah. They ask him to pray that the LORD will show them the way. They promise to obey, whether the answer is pleasant or not. After ten days the word comes. If they stay in the land, God will build them up and plant them. They need not fear the king of Babylon. If they go to Egypt, the sword and famine will follow them there. Jeremiah says they deceived themselves when they asked.
chapters.43.summary: The officers tell Jeremiah he is lying. They say Baruch has turned him against them. They lead all the people into Egypt, with Jeremiah and Baruch. They settle at Tahpanhes. There the LORD tells Jeremiah to bury large stones at the entrance to Pharaoh’s house. Nebuchadnezzar will set his throne over those stones. He will strike Egypt and burn the houses of its gods.
chapters.44.summary: The LORD’s word comes to the Jews living across Egypt. They have seen Jerusalem ruined because of offerings to other gods. Jeremiah asks why they repeat that sin in Egypt. The men and women answer that they will not listen. They will keep burning incense to the queen of the sky. When they did so in Judah, they had food and safety. Since they stopped, they have lacked everything. Jeremiah answers that the LORD remembered those offerings, and events will show whose word stands.
chapters.45.summary: This short word is for Baruch, Jeremiah’s scribe. It dates from the year he wrote the scroll. Baruch has said that the LORD added sorrow to his pain. He is worn out and finds no rest. The LORD says he is tearing down what he built across the whole land. He asks whether Baruch seeks great things for himself. Baruch should not seek them. He will keep his life wherever he goes.
chapters.46.summary: This is the first of Jeremiah’s messages about foreign nations. Egypt’s army is defeated at Carchemish by the king of Babylon. Its soldiers are terrified and fall back. Egypt rose like the Nile and said it would cover the earth. No medicine will heal it. A second message says Nebuchadnezzar will invade Egypt itself. Pharaoh is called a loud noise who missed his moment. Afterward Egypt will be lived in again, and Jacob need not fear.
chapters.47.summary: This message concerns the Philistines. Waters rise from the north and become an overflowing flood. People cry out at the sound of horses and chariots. Fathers are too weak to turn back for their children. Tyre and Sidon lose their last helpers. Gaza and Ashkelon are silenced. A voice asks how long the LORD’s sword will keep striking. The answer is that the LORD has given it an order.
chapters.48.summary: This long message concerns Moab. Its towns are named one by one as they fall. Its god Chemosh goes into exile with his priests. Moab has been at ease since its youth, like wine left undisturbed. It mocked Israel and was very proud. The speaker wails for Moab and weeps for its vineyards. Joy and gladness are gone from its fields. Yet the LORD will restore Moab’s fortunes in the last days.
chapters.49.summary: This chapter gathers messages about five peoples. Ammon trusted in its treasures and will see its capital ruined. Edom trusted in its wisdom and its high cliffs. Damascus grows weak, and its young men fall in the streets. The desert tribes of Kedar lose their tents and camels. Elam’s bow is broken, and its people are scattered. Ammon and Elam are promised restoration afterward. God says he will keep Edom’s orphans alive.
chapters.50.summary: This message announces the fall of Babylon. Its gods are put to shame, and a nation from the north attacks. Israel and Judah come weeping and ask the way to Zion. They have been lost sheep, misled by their shepherds. Their enemies said harming them was no crime, since they had sinned. Assyria devoured Israel, and Babylon gnawed its bones. God will punish Babylon as he punished Assyria. The hammer of the whole earth is broken.
chapters.51.summary: The LORD will send a destroying wind against Babylon. Babylon was a golden cup that made the whole earth drunk. Now it falls suddenly, and its wound cannot be healed. The LORD made the earth by his power, and idols are nothing. Zion says Nebuchadnezzar swallowed her like a monster. Babylon’s thick walls will be leveled. Jeremiah writes all this in a scroll and gives it to an officer named Seraiah. Seraiah must read it in Babylon and sink it in the Euphrates.
chapters.52.summary: This last chapter retells the fall of Jerusalem. Zedekiah rebels, and Babylon besieges the city until the food is gone. The wall is breached, and the king is caught and blinded. The temple, the palace, and the houses are burned. The bronze pillars and vessels of the temple are carried away. The chief priests and officials are executed. The numbers of the exiles are listed. Years later the king of Babylon frees Jehoiachin and feeds him at his table.
